text:
B: Oh. Hello. Sorry, it took a second to connect.
A: Hiya. You're alright.
B: Erm, I'm Joanne.
A: Donna.
B: Hello.
A: So… do we just talk then?
B: I think so. Three minutes, it said.
A: Right.
B: Erm, where are you, then?
A: Plumstead. South-east London. You?
B: Crawley.
A: Oh, near Gatwick.
B: Yeah, right under it, sort of. The planes have been ever so loud lately.
A: I bet.
B: Do you, erm… do you do a lot of these? The studies?
A: Yeah, a few. Bit of extra money, isn't it. I'm not working at the minute, so.
B: No, me neither, actually. I was made redundant last year. I'd been at the same place seventeen years.
A: Seventeen years? That's harsh. What was it?
B: Accounts. At a builders' merchants. They got bought out and moved everything up to Milton Keynes.
A: Did they not give you the option?
B: They did, but I wasn't going to move to Milton Keynes. I live with my mum and dad, so.
A: Yeah, no, fair enough. I was cleaning, offices in Woolwich, early mornings. Contract ended. I liked it to be fair, nobody about, headphones in, just get on with it.
B: That sounds nice, actually. I'd rather that than the phones.
A: Yeah, I can't be doing with phones.
B: No.
A: …
B: Erm, did you do the puzzle bit alright?
A: Sort of. I got bored halfway through, if I'm honest.
B: I quite liked it. I do word searches and that, so.
A: Fair enough.
B: Have you got any pets? I've got a Jack Russell, Bobby. He's quite old now, his back leg's not great.
A: No. We're in a flat, it's not really allowed. I've got two kids though, that's enough.
B: How old are they?
A: Kyle's sixteen, he's doing his GCSEs this year. And Mia's eleven, she's just started secondary. Lost her blazer already. First month.
B: Oh no.
A: Yeah. Forty quid, them blazers. And Kyle's on his PlayStation till all hours, I keep telling him, you've got exams, you was up till two last night. Do you know what I mean? I just want him to sort of get his head down. Do better than I did.
B: Yeah. I'm sure he will.
A: Hope so. Have you got kids?
B: No. No, I haven't.
A: Right.
B: Erm. Do you watch any of the soaps?
A: EastEnders. Every night, pretty much.
B: I'm more Corrie. And Emmerdale. My mum and I watch them after dinner.
A: My mum's Corrie. She rings me about it, she rings me about everything, five times a day.
B: Mine's in the next room, so she just shouts.
A: Ha. That's worse, to be fair.
B: It is a bit, yeah.
